consultations.purpose: Trace the Latin reception of covenant and testament terminology without treating the Vulgate as textual or lexical authority for LPF.
queryScope: normalized nominative foedus and prefix foeder-
consultations.method: Full normalized surface scan of the 73 pinned Latin files; Windows-1252 ligatures normalized only for discovery; every result retains printed surface and verse line.
consultations.resultSummary: 432 formal candidates: 103 testament-, 109 pact-, 83 foedus, and 137 foeder-. The NT has 33 testament- surfaces, matching the 33 TR1894 occurrences of diatheke; Hebrews uses testamentum continuously across covenant, ark/tablets, 9:15-17, blood, and new/eternal covenant contexts. No Spanish equivalent was assigned.

consultations.purpose: Trace the Latin reception of Hades, Gehenna, and Tartarus terminology without treating the Vulgate as textual or lexical authority for LPF.
queryScope: manual cross-check of all NT gehenna surfaces
manual cross-check of in tartarum at 2 Peter 2:4
consultations.method: Full normalized surface scan of the 73 pinned Latin files for infern-; Windows-1252 ligatures normalized only for discovery; every result retains printed surface and verse line; Gehenna and Tartarus forms cross-checked in the same pinned text.
consultations.resultSummary: 69 infern- surfaces in 68 verses. The NT uses infernus for Hades, preserves all 12 Gehenna occurrences as gehenna forms, and preserves the Tartarus verb at 2 Peter 2:4 with in tartarum tradidit; Latin reception therefore did not simply collapse all source terms into infernus.

consultations.purpose: Trace the Latin reception of Hebrew nephesh and Greek psyche without treating the Vulgate as textual or lexical authority for LPF.
queryScope: normalized exact singular forms of anima
normalized exact plural forms of anima
consultations.method: Full normalized exact-form scan of the 73 pinned Latin files; animal-family derivatives excluded; Windows-1252 ligatures normalized only for discovery; every result retains printed surface and verse line.
consultations.resultSummary: 911 anima surfaces in 848 verses. The same Latin family spans body-soul contrast, life surrendered or endangered, numbered persons, living creatures, inner disposition, and postmortem identity; no Spanish equivalent was assigned.

consultations.purpose: Trace the Latin reception of Hebrew and Greek salvation terminology without treating the Vulgate as textual or lexical authority for LPF.
queryScope: normalized exact inflectional forms of salus and salutaris
normalized exact inflectional forms of salvus, salvare, salvatio, and salvator
consultations.method: Full normalized exact-form scan of the 73 pinned Latin files; Windows-1252 ligatures normalized only for discovery; every result retains printed surface and verse line; salutare and salutes homographs remain visible for contextual review.
consultations.resultSummary: 684 exact-form surfaces in 646 verses. Latin reception uses salus/salutare and salvus/salvare/salvator across physical rescue, safety, healing, historical deliverance, and theological salvation; greeting homographs show why Latin form alone cannot decide the Spanish.

consultations.purpose: Trace Latin reception of worship, homage, and service terminology without treating the Vulgate as textual or lexical authority for LPF.
queryScope: normalized exact verbal forms of servire
consultations.method: Full normalized scan of the 73 pinned Latin files; every result retains printed surface and verse line; one adornatus false positive remains visible; no Spanish equivalent was assigned.
consultations.resultSummary: 566 surfaces in 506 verses: 281 ador- candidates and 285 exact servire verbal forms. Matthew 4:10 and Luke 4:8 preserve the Greek distinction with adorabis and servies rather than collapsing both verbs into one Latin family.

consultations.purpose: Trace Latin reception of ekklesia and neighboring assembly families without treating the Vulgate as textual or lexical authority for LPF.
queryScope: normalized prefixes ecclesi-, congreg-, synagog-, and concili-
consultations.method: Full normalized surface scan of the 73 pinned Latin files; every result retains printed surface and verse line; no Spanish equivalent was assigned.
consultations.resultSummary: 717 surfaces in 689 verses: 170 ecclesi-, 435 congreg-, 78 synagog-, and 34 concili-. Latin keeps ecclesia even for the confused and lawful civic assembly in Acts 19, showing formal continuity rather than a ready-made Spanish semantic decision.

consultations.purpose: Trace Latin reception of baptism, immersion, dipping, and washing families without treating the Vulgate as lexical authority for LPF.
queryScope: normalized prefixes bapt-, merg-, ting-, and lav-
consultations.method: Full normalized surface scan of 73 pinned Latin files; every result retains verse context; no Spanish equivalent was assigned.
consultations.resultSummary: 249 surfaces in 219 verses: 117 bapt-, 6 merg-, 11 ting-, and 115 lav-. Latin reception normally transliterates the ritual family while retaining separate immersion, dipping, and washing vocabulary.

consultations.purpose: Trace Latin reception of apostle, envoy, sending, and messenger families without treating the Vulgate as lexical authority for LPF.
queryScope: normalized prefixes legat-, miss-, and nunti-
consultations.method: Full normalized surface scan of 73 pinned Latin files; every result retains verse context; transliterated apostle forms remain separate from legate, sending, and messenger controls.
consultations.resultSummary: 523 surfaces in 490 verses: 85 exact apostol- forms, 32 legat-, 85 miss-, and 321 nunti-. Latin preserves apostolus even in John 13:16, 2 Corinthians 8:23, and Philippians 2:25, extending the transliteration to ordinary commissioned envoys.
